title: A Vaccine for Epstein-Barr Virus: Gary Nabel on The Long Run - TimmermanReport.com
gist: ModeX Therapeutics, founded by former Sanofi CSO Gary Nabel on a multi-specific antibody platform first built at Sanofi, is running the first-ever Epstein-Barr Virus vaccine candidate through clinical trials with partner Merck, betting that EBV reactivation is a hidden contributor to several cancers, multiple sclerosis, and autoimmune disease.

themes.theme: ModeX's platform bet on Epstein-Barr Virus

insights.claim: ModeX Therapeutics, led by CEO and co-founder Gary Nabel, is developing a multi-specific biologics platform originally built on work started at Sanofi when Nabel was the company's chief scientific officer, with its lead program a vaccine against Epstein-Barr Virus currently in clinical trials, partnered with Merck.
insights.speaker: Timmerman Report
insights.so_what: A clinical-stage EBV vaccine partnered with Merck is a concrete near-term catalyst to track for both ModeX and Merck's vaccine pipeline, given no EBV vaccine currently exists on the market.
insights.quote: The company has a platform for making multi-specific biologics into vaccines and cancer treatments. ModeX was founded in 2020, building on work that started at Sanofi when Nabel was the chief scientific officer there.

insights.claim: There is currently no vaccine against Epstein-Barr Virus, and while ModeX's candidate still has a long way to go through clinical development, success could theoretically prevent a substantial burden of debilitating chronic disease linked to the virus.
insights.speaker: Timmerman Report
insights.so_what: The 'no existing vaccine, long way to go' framing signals this is a high-risk, high-reward, still-early-stage biotech bet rather than a near-term approvable asset — appropriate to track but not yet de-risked.
insights.quote: There is no vaccine against the virus, and the ModeX candidate still has a long way to go. But if ModeX and its partner, Merck. are successful, it could theoretically prevent a lot of debilitating chronic diseases.

insights.claim: Epstein-Barr Virus, which causes infectious mononucleosis and lies dormant in most adults, can be reactivated later in life and is increasingly implicated as a contributing factor in several types of cancer, multiple sclerosis, and other autoimmune diseases.
insights.speaker: Timmerman Report
insights.so_what: A broadening causal link between EBV reactivation and major chronic disease categories (cancer, MS, autoimmune) significantly expands the addressable clinical and commercial rationale for an EBV vaccine well beyond preventing acute mononucleosis.
insights.quote: what has become clearer in recent years is that EBV, which lays dormant in most adults, can be reactivated later in life and cause a lot of other problems. EBV is implicated as a culprit in several types of cancer, multiple sclerosis, and autoimmune diseases.

insights.claim: ModeX applies the same multi-specific antibody engineering platform not only to its EBV vaccine but also to spur an immune response against cancer and to treat or prevent COVID-19, reflecting a platform-technology strategy rather than a single-asset bet.
insights.speaker: Timmerman Report
insights.so_what: A platform that can be pointed at multiple indications (infectious disease, oncology, another infectious disease) diversifies ModeX's shots-on-goal versus a company built around one drug candidate, relevant to how investors should weight binary clinical-trial risk in this name.
insights.quote: ModeX is using the same technology toolkit to spur an immune response against cancer and to treat or prevent COVID-19.

insights.claim: Gary Nabel's career path — starting as a virologist, then holding senior scientific positions at the NIH and as chief scientific officer at Sanofi, before founding ModeX — reflects a recurring biotech pattern of deep pharma/public-sector R&D leaders spinning out underexploited internal research into independent platform-focused startups.
insights.speaker: Timmerman Report
insights.so_what: This founder-background pattern (senior pharma R&D leader spinning out platform technology developed internally) is a recognizable and often-successful biotech startup archetype worth factoring into diligence on founder-led platform companies.
insights.quote: Gary's career, starting as a virologist, then taking senior scientific positions at the NIH and Sanofi, has ended up leading down this very interesting startup path.

insights.claim: AlphaSense's healthcare research team frames 2026 as a year of transition for healthcare and life sciences, citing high-stakes battles for new drug markets such as oral GLP-1s and targeted radioligand therapies, alongside a resurgent biotech IPO market, as the major themes of its first-half Sector Spotlight series.
insights.speaker: Timmerman Report
insights.so_what: Positions the EBV vaccine story within a broader 2026 narrative of active drug-market competition (GLP-1s, radioligand therapies) and a reopening biotech IPO window, useful context for sector-wide capital flow tracking even though it is sponsor-supplied content.
insights.quote: So far 2026 has been a year of transition for healthcare and life sciences... featuring the high-stakes battles for new drug markets (like oral GLP-1s and targeted radioligand therapies), a resurgent biotech IPO market, and more.
